title: Per-answer timing floor cut from /apply's 2s to 500ms (spec decision 12) leaves the AD-15 timing check filtering only sub-500ms scripted replays on the JS autosave path
evidence:
12. **Per-question timing floor is 500ms, not the /apply 2s (AC6 adaptation).** The form page renders every question at one load, so a fast first tap legitimately lands inside 2s of the stamp; a 2s floor would silently eat it (the fake-advance drops the answer). Answer POST/PUTs keep every fail-closed branch (missing / unparseable / future / >7d) with a 500ms scripted-replay floor; the single-action resend POST keeps the full 2s `is_timing_suspicious` unchanged. Flagged for Perkins.

AC6 baseline: Given the answer/resend POSTs, when they arrive, then the honeypot field (`_website`) and timing validation (`_form_loaded_at`, <2s or >7d suspicious — `application_handler` helpers reused as-is) apply.
detail: On the JS path all questions share one page-load `_form_loaded_at` (reference_form.js sends every answer as a PUT against that single stamp), so a scripted replay spacing PUTs >=500ms passes every timing check; /apply's 2s floor would have caught sub-2s bursts. Fail-closed branches remain, but discrimination is near-zero.
recommended_fix: Confirm the tradeoff explicitly, or restore the 2s floor for the first answer after page load and re-stamp the timing field when the stepper reveals each question, keeping per-question pacing measurable on the JS path.
